item.title: IRGC Navy official violating vessels in Hormuz Strait 'punished every night'
item.description:
IRGC Navy official violating vessels in Hormuz Strait 'punished every night'

The political deputy of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said that its forces have been carrying out nightly operations in the Strait of Hormuz targeting what it considers as violating vessels. 

"Every night, from the beginning of the war until now, the IRGC Navy has carried out these operations to protect the country’s interests," Ali Mohammadi told the Fars news agency.

"The IRGC Navy has had complete and absolute surveillance over the Strait of Hormuz from the first day of the war," he added, saying that its troops can "impose its will" on ships it deems to have violated its rules.

item.title: Trump rules out new attack on Iran until after midterms as oil prices spike
item.description:
Trump rules out new attack on Iran until after midterms as oil prices spike

US President Donald Trump on Thursday ruled out new attacks on Iran until after the November mid-term elections, following several reports that Washington is gearing up for a new round of escalation.

"We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd.”

Trump’s statement came after several news sites, including Axios, which is seen as close to Trump and his aides, reported that the Pentagon was preparing for a resumption of high-intensity strikes on Iran. The Atlantic also reported Trump is weighing attacking Iran before the US midterm elections.

Read more: Trump rules out new attack on Iran until after midterms as oil prices spike

item.title: Over 200 organisations set to join 'Global Day of Action' for Palestine
item.description:
Over 200 organisations set to join 'Global Day of Action' for Palestine

Submitted by Mera Aladam on Fri, 10/09/2026 - 03:58
The mass pro-Palestine protests on Saturday will take place across 60 countries in over 250 locations worldwide
Protestors attend a pro-Palestinian demonstration on the third anniversary of Israel's genocide in Gaza, in Berlin, Germany on 7 October, 2026 (Christian Mang/Reuters)
Off

More than 200 organisations across the globe will be mobilising for mass pro-Palestine protests on Saturday, the Global Alliance for Palestine (GAFP) announced on Wednesday. 

According to the statement, the organisations will "execute a synchronised Global Day of Action", and are set to include civil society groups, trade unions, student federations and human rights networks across 60 countries.

The event is organised by GAFP alongside the Anti-Apartheid Movement (AAM) and SANED (Global Coalition against Occupation of Palestine).

"As governments actively fund, arm, and protect Israel from any legal accountability, grassroots movements are refusing to allow this genocide to become normalised as the status quo," GAFP wrote. 

It added that the event "marks a decisive shift, moving beyond symbolic protest toward direct civil intervention to shut down public complicity and demand systemic accountability for Israel’s war crimes and genocide".

Anas Altikriti, Secretary-General of the Global Alliance for Palestine, said that the third anniversary marking Israel's continued genocide in Gaza is a "stark, devastating reminder of the unbearable terror and suffering that the
Palestinian people have been forced to endure every single day for three years".

"As world powers remain silent and complicit, civil society is rising," he added, saying that the global demonstration is a a direct response to "this ongoing horror".

Altikriti went on to describe the event as a "declaration that the global conscience will not stand idly by as a genocide is normalised."

Our interactive map shows the scale and diversity of this weekend’s Global Day of Action for Palestine. More than 300 actions across 60+ countries, united around two demands: End the Genocide. Defend the Land. Explore the map: https://t.co/bvAZtd6PQw https://t.co/OIvoQ5lZWv

— Global Alliance For Palestine (@ga4palestine) October 7, 2026

"We are taking to the streets to demand total accountability, an immediate end to the siege, and a free Palestine."

Demand for Palestinian liberation, end to genocide

GAFP stressed that the global mobilisation on Saturday is "not a passive memorial for three years of genocide", but is instead a "direct action to halt the machinery that enables Israel's violence".

Participating organisations in over 250 locations worldwide are expected to shut down civic squares, encircle government buildings and blockade corporate entities directly tied to military supply chains.

Three years of death and devastation: Israel's war on Gaza in pictures
Read More »

"The objective is clear: render normal commerce and political diplomacy impossible while Israel’s genocide continues uninterrupted."

According to the press release, the mass protests are set to take place in cities such as London, Sydney, Berlin, Brussels, Prague, Reykjavik, Athens, Modena, Sao Paulo, Mexico City, Kuala Lumpur and Johannesburg. 

Meanwhile, in cities like Athens and Modena, the coalition indicated that "actions will extend across multiple days with cultural sit-ins, public teach-ins, and large-scale visual projections highlighting Israel’s war crimes directly onto government and corporate buildings".

"Three years into Israel's genocide, the global movement for Palestine has grown in power, unity, and resolve," the statement added.

"As the October 10 Global Day of Action approaches, millions around the world across every continent are sending an unmistakable message: the demand for Palestinian liberation, land protection, and an immediate end to Israel's genocide and occupation will no longer wait on international permission - it is taking to the streets to enforce it."

Israeli forces kill at least seven Palestinians in separate attacks across Gaza
item.description:
Israeli forces kill at least seven Palestinians in separate attacks across Gaza

At least seven Palestinians, including a child, were killed in separate Israeli strikes throughout the day, Gaza’s civil defence rescue service said on Thursday.

Strikes were reported in Gaza City, the al-Sudaniya area, al-Mawasi in Rafah, Bani Suheila, and northeastern Khan Younis.

Gaza’s health ministry said that as of Thursday, Israeli violations of the ceasefire agreement had killed 1,471 Palestinians and injured 5,189 others.

Since October 2023, Israel has killed over 74,254 Palestinians in the besieged enclave. Thousands more remain missing, likely buried beneath the rubble.

item.description: At the beginning of October  2026, Israel refused to allow officials from the Palestinian Central Elections Commission and international election observers to enter Gaza to monitor preparations for the legislative elections. item.title: Israeli army shells outskirts of village in southern Syria
item.description: The Israeli army fired an artillery shell toward the outskirts of a village in Syria’s southern Quneitra province Thursday, Syrian media reported. State-run Alikhbariah TV said Israeli forces targeted the vicinity of Sweisa village in the southern Quneitra countryside. No casualties or damage were immediately reported. The shelling came amid continued Israeli military incursions and attacks in southern Syria. Earlier Thursday, Israeli forces advanced into the village of Al-Samdaniya Al-Sharqiya in Quneitra province with two tanks and more than 15 military vehicles carrying soldiers, Alikhbariah TV reported. The forces moved toward the outskirts of Tal Krum, the broadcaster said.
